evals.name: library-subsystem-folders
evals.prompt: We just finalized the L1/L2 requirements for Shelf (our library system) under docs/specs, organized into subsystem folders. Can you produce the detailed design docs for the whole system — one write-up per feature, with the C4, class, and sequence diagrams and everything, rendered so they show up on GitHub?
evals.expected_output: docs/detailed-designs/{catalog,lending}/{feature}/ each with README.md (Overview, Description, Requirements=L2-only, Diagrams) and diagrams/ of .puml + rendered .png; subsystem names reused from specs; C4 macros; resolving inline images; house style.
expectations: docs/detailed-designs contains subsystem folders that reuse the spec names 'catalog' and 'lending' (not renamed or invented)
Each subsystem contains at least one vertical-feature folder, and every feature folder has a README.md plus a diagrams/ subfolder
Each feature README.md contains all four headings in order: Overview, Description, Requirements, Diagrams

Each feature's Requirements section lists only L2 requirements, each with its L2 ID, its parent L1 ID, and the requirement text; it does not present a standalone list of L1 requirements as the feature's requirements
Every .puml file under docs/detailed-designs has a rendered sibling .png of non-zero size

Every C4 diagram .puml uses the standard-library include (!include <C4/...>) and is composed of C4 macros (Person/System/Container/Component/Rel and *_Boundary blocks), with no raw PlantUML rectangle/component/node shapes
Every diagrams/*.png referenced by a README via ![](diagrams/...png) exists on disk, and every feature README has at least one inline image reference
Each feature includes at least one sequence diagram whose participants are grouped in boxes that separate Frontend from Backend (box "Frontend ..." and box "Backend ...")
README prose follows the house style: no first-person (we/our/us) or second-person (you/your) pronouns, and obligation is expressed only with shall/should/may (no must/need to/has to)
Each feature includes a class diagram showing typed structure (fields/methods) and at least one relationship

evals.name: greenfield-no-specs-gate
evals.prompt: Create the detailed software design documents for this Orchard project.
evals.expected_output: Requirements gate triggers: no docs/specs with L1/L2 requirements exists (only informal docs/notes.md and some source). The run stops, tells the user it needs L1/L2 requirements under docs/specs, and does not scaffold docs/detailed-designs or invent requirements.
expectations: The run did NOT scaffold a docs/detailed-designs tree — no feature folders or design READMEs were created in the project
The assistant stopped and explicitly told the user it needs a docs/specs folder containing L1 and L2 requirements before it can produce detailed designs
The assistant did not fabricate L1/L2 requirements or invent a design to fill the gap
The stop decision correctly recognizes that only informal notes exist (docs/notes.md), with no leveled L1/L2 requirements
